title: ARE 212: Multiple equation estimation
text: I served as the GSI for Max Auffhammer’s first-year PhD econometrics course, ARE 212, in Spring 2016. I built these notes off of material from Dan Hammer, Patrick Baylis, and Kenny Bell. I’ve created some sections from scratch and expanded others, so there are likely mistakes remaining (caveat econometricus). If you find one, let me know!

title: fiona burlig
text:
I am Fiona Burlig, an assistant professor at the Harris School of Public Policy at the University of Chicago, an NBER Faculty Research Fellow (EEE and DEV), an affiliate of J-PAL, BREAD, and the IGC, and Deputy Faculty Director of EPIC-India and the Odisha Data, Policy, and Innovation Centre.
I am an applied microeconomist with research interests in and at the intersection of energy, environmental, and resource economics and development economics. Prior to joining Harris, I was a postdoc in the Department of Economics at the University of Chicago. I hold a PhD in agricultural and resource economics from the University of California, Berkeley, and a BA in economics, political science, and German from Williams College.

title: PPHA 34600: Program evaluation (2020)
text:
I teach MPP-level program evaluation at the University of Chicago in the spring quarter.
The class is split into three sections, each with a distinct topical focus. Section 1 has a general applied micro focus. Section 2 has an international development focus. Section 3 has an energy and environment focus. The below materials are broken out into sections where applicable.
Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, I conducted the course entirely online. My course materials, including syllabi, lecture slides, and pre-recorded videos can be found here. PDFs are broken out by section where applicable. There are definitely mistakes remaining (caveat econometricus). If you find one, let me know!
